10	/-!
11	# B-5 step 3: the vanishing threshold at the splitting field is UNIFORM, and it is π-free
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` settles that at a chart index legal at parameter
14	`n` the coverage hypothesis `hb` of `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` forces `b = n`, and
15	that `b = g` is false in general (`hb_forces_h0_eq_one`).  Its item 3 then names the residue:
16	*reconcile the chart parameter with the threshold*.  Both that file and
17	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`'s retraction treat the threshold `b` — DAT-0a's bound
18	**at the splitting field `L`** — as a per-`L` quantity that has to be obtained before the
19	reconciliation can even be stated.
20	
21	**That is where the pricing is wrong, and this file measures why.**  Two separate points:
22	
23	* **DAT-0a itself is not instantiable at `L`, and that is not an obstruction.**
24	  `exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`
25	  (`RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean:71`) carries `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` with `[IsFinite π]`,
26	  `[IsDominant π]` and `hπ`.  There is no `relCurve C L ⟶ P1 L` anywhere in this tree, so a
27	  lane trying to instantiate DAT-0a at a splitting field is trying to build a morphism the
28	  project does not have.  This is presumably why no coverage file ever cited a threshold at
29	  `L`.
30	* **The threshold does not need DAT-0a.**  `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_witness`
31	  (`RiemannRoch/WindowFieldTransport.lean:87`) is the **π-free peeling**: a *single* witness
32	  divisor with vanishing `H¹` gives vanishing for every divisor of degree
33	  `≥ deg W₀ + 1 − χ`.  And `windowN C L hπ g` (`:307`) is such a witness on `relCurve C L`
34	  for every field extension `L/k`, with `subsingleton_h1_windowN` and
35	  `deg_windowN = M·δ`.
36	
37	## The consequence, and it is the point of the file
38	
39	The bound that comes out is `windowM_choice π hπ g * windowδ π + g`, in which **`L` does not
40	occur**: `windowM_choice` and `windowδ` are ledger constants of the *base* field `k` (see
41	I-0204 — the per-field ledger constants do not transport, which is exactly why the window
42	lane transports window *facts* instead, and why the transported witness carries a `k`-level
43	degree).  So the threshold is **uniform across all splitting fields**, and the "which
44	threshold at which fibre" half of the reconciliation is not a residue at all.
45	
46	What that buys, precisely: `index_of_threshold`
47	(`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean:147`) already realises *any* `b ≥ 0` as the ledger
48	value of a legal chart index at parameter `b.toNat`.  What it could not be composed with was a
49	`b` known to exist at the splitting field.  Now it can, at one `b` for all fibres.
50	
51	## What this does NOT do, stated plainly
52	
53	* **It closes no antecedent of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.**  Coverage still owes the
54	  *existence of the chart point*, i.e. the pointwise datum of
55	  `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`; this file supplies one hypothesis of one theorem on the
56	  route to the locus-membership half.
57	* **`hb_forces_h0_eq_one` stands.**  The threshold here is `M·δ + g`, which for `M ≥ 1` and
58	  `δ ≥ 1` is strictly above `g`; it is *not* a route to `b = g`, and nothing here weakens that
59	  refutation.  What it says is that the chart parameter has to be `(M·δ + g)`, not `g` — and
60	  since `n` is free throughout the chart layer (`Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s own
61	  correction, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`'s heterogeneity), that is a *statement about which
62	  parameter the atlas is indexed at*, which is addressed to the divRep lane.
63	* **It is not new geometry.**  Every ingredient was landed; `windowN` and
64	  `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_witness` have zero occurrences in any `Pic0Chart*` file, so
65	  this is a cross-layer citation that nobody had made.
66	
67	## Main declarations
68	
69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_h1_of_ledger_bound` — **the uniform threshold at an
70	  arbitrary field extension**: every divisor on `relCurve C L` of degree `≥ M·δ + g` has
71	  vanishing `H¹`, with `L` occurring in neither the bound nor any hypothesis but the tower.
72	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_uniform_bound_forall_baseChange` — the same read as DAT-0a's own
73	  `∃ b`-shape, with the `∃` **outside** the quantifier over `L`.  This is the statement the
74	  coverage layer's "per-fibre threshold" pricing assumed to be unavailable.
75	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_ledger_bound` — coverage's locus membership with the
76	  threshold hypothesis **discharged**, leaving `hdeg` (the calibration) as the only numeric
77	  input.
78	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chartIndex_mem_chartLocus_of_ledger_bound` — the composite with
79	  `index_of_threshold`'s direction: at the ledger parameter there is a legal chart index whose
80	  locus contains the point.
81	-/

125	`L/k`, with the same bound.

127	Read the bound: `windowM_choice π hπ g` and `windowδ π` are ledger constants of the *base*
128	field, so `L` occurs nowhere in it.  That is what makes this uniform, and it is the fact the
129	coverage layer's pricing of its own residue assumed to be unavailable
130	(`Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` item 3, `Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`'s retraction: both

134	(`exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) needs a finite dominant
135	`relCurve C L ⟶ P1 L` and this tree has none.  Instead
136	`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_witness` peels from a single witness, and the witness is the
137	transported window divisor `windowN C L hπ g` whose vanishing is `subsingleton_h1_windowN`

140	theorem subsingleton_h1_of_ledger_bound {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
141	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : ℕ)
142	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
143	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
144	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
145	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
146	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
147	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
148	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]

167	them.
168

170	residue was priced against, and having it as an `∃` makes the comparison mechanical rather
171	than a reading of two docstrings.  The witness is the ledger value, which is why it does not

173	theorem exists_uniform_bound_forall_baseChange {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
174	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : ℕ)
175	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ)) :
176	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L),
177	      ∀ (_ : IsIntegral (relCurve C L))
178	        (_ : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)))
179	        (_ : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)))
180	        (_ : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0))
181	        (_ : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)),
182	      ∀ D : (relCurve C L).CurveDivisor, b ≤ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D →
183	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).divisorSheaf L D) 1) :=
184	  ⟨(windowM_choice π hπ g : ℤ) * windowδ π + (g : ℤ),
185	    fun L _ _ _ _ _ _ _ D hD => subsingleton_h1_of_ledger_bound hπ g hχ L D hD⟩

187	/-! ## Coverage with the threshold discharged
188	
189	`mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean:154`) takes `hb`
190	(the threshold) and `hdeg` (the calibration).  The threshold is now available at the
191	splitting field, so the composite below carries only the calibration — which is what
192	`Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s `index_of_threshold` is about. -/
193	
194	/-- **Coverage's locus membership with the threshold hypothesis DISCHARGED.**
195	
196	Verbatim `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` with `hb` supplied by
197	`subsingleton_h1_of_ledger_bound` at the ledger bound, so the only numeric input left is

200	Note what remains and what does not.  Gone: the per-fibre existence of a threshold, which the
201	coverage prose treated as the blocker.  Still here: `hdeg`, and by `ledger_forces_b_eq_n` that

232	
233	`mem_chartLocus_of_ledger_bound` still carries `hdeg`.  But `hdeg` is not an independent
234	obligation: `classDeg_presenting_twist` (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean:124`)
235	computes the presenting class's degree as `m·d₁ − deg_k Z` from the degree-zero-ness of `λ` at
236	the point, so the constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − (M·δ + g)` — a chart index legal at the ledger
237	parameter, in the sense of `index_of_threshold` — supplies it outright. -/
238	
239	/-- **COVERAGE AT THE LEDGER PARAMETER, WITH BOTH NUMERIC INPUTS DISCHARGED.**
240	
241	Given only: `λ` of fibre degree zero at the point, a splitting `M₀` of its fibre class, and a
242	chart index legal at the **ledger parameter** `M·δ + g` (i.e. `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − (M·δ + g)`),
243	the point lies in the chart locus.
244	
245	Compare `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound`, whose two numeric hypotheses were `hb` (the
246	threshold) and `hdeg` (the calibration).  Both are gone: `hb` by
247	`subsingleton_h1_of_ledger_bound` — the uniform π-free threshold — and `hdeg` by
248	`classDeg_presenting_twist` from the index constraint.  What remains is *only* the splitting
249	and the degree-zero-ness, which coverage has (`exists_splitting_of_picEt`,
250	`Pic0ChartSplit.lean:143`, and the `pic0Subgroup` membership of the class).
251	
252	**This is the reduction, and it is worth being exact about its scope.**  It is
253	locus-membership at a point of a test, at ONE chart parameter, and it says nothing about the
254	pointwise datum `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` needs — that also wants a chart POINT over a
255	neighbourhood, i.e. the divisor family whose class is `λ`, which is the spreading-out
256	`Pic0ChartCoverageSlice.lean` records as absent for this carrier.  So antecedent 2 is not
257	closed and I claim nothing on it.  What is closed is that the *numeric* half of B-5 step 3 —
258	which two files and the `dat-b` row present as the open question — has no content left.
259	
260	The parameter is `M·δ + g`, not `g`: `hb_forces_h0_eq_one` is untouched, and this route

281	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
282	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]

288	  -- morphism (`relCurveMap_eq_overSpecMap_ofId`), but not syntactically.

311	    (hlam : degAt lam (Over.testPoint t) = 0)
312	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)

314	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
315	        - ((windowM_choice π hπ g : ℤ) * windowδ π + (g : ℤ)))

318	    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L]

name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

the vanishing to `W₀ + E`, and witness-independence
(`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`) reaches `D`. -/
theorem subsingleton_hModule_one_of_witness (W₀ D : Y.CurveDivisor)
    (hW₀ : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W₀) 1))
    (hdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K W₀ + 1 - Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K)
      ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D) 1) := by

  have hWcdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K Wc
      = CurveDivisor.deg K D - CurveDivisor.deg K W₀ := by
    rw [← classDeg_picClass K Wc, hWc, hc, classDeg_mul, classDeg_inv,
      classDeg_picClass, classDeg_picClass]
    ring
  have hWdeg : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K Wc + Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) := by
    rw [hWcdeg]; linarith
  obtain ⟨E, hE0, hEc⟩ := exists_effective_of_picClass Wc hWdeg
  have hclass : CurveDivisor.picClass K (W₀ + E) = CurveDivisor.picClass K D := by
    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, hEc, hWc, hc,
      mul_comm (CurveDivisor.picClass K D), ← mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel, one_mul]
  exact subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq K hclass
    (peel_effective W₀ E hE0 hW₀)

end Peeling

# DAT-0a — the P5-uniform `H¹`-vanishing bound

For the curve bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one, locally of finite type
and quasi-compact over a field `K`) carrying a **finite dominant** morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`,
there is a single integer threshold `b`, depending only on `(Y, π)` and quantified over **all**
Weil divisors `D`, past which the degree-one cohomology of `𝒪(D)` vanishes:

`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`:
`∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`.

This is the **P5-uniform** pre-brick of the Wave-4 datum campaign (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md`
§2.1, §4 DAT-0a). It is consumed by DAT-D's uniform Grassmannian twist, where the twist exponent
`M` is chosen so that `deg (Θ^M) ≥ b` and the whole degree-`g` family lands in the vanishing
locus.

## The route (worksheet §4 DAT-0a, collapsed form)

The proof is the FLV-class argument (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`) with the twist specialized to the
fiber divisor `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` and the base twist fixed at the FLV-fiber threshold `n₁` of
`D₀ = 0`:

* FLV-fiber at `D₀ = 0` (`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) gives `n₁` with
  `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n·F))` for all `n ≥ n₁`; take `n = n₁`, so the base twist `n₁·F` is fixed;
* `0 < deg F` (`zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor`) makes `b := n₁·deg F + 1 − χ(𝒪_Y)` a legal
  threshold: for `deg D ≥ b` the residual class `[D]·[F]^{-n₁}` has degree `≥ 1 − χ`, so
  `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields an **effective** witness `E` of that class;
* `n₁·F + E` is in the class of `D`; `peel_effective` transports `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F))` to
  `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F + E))`, and witness-independence
  (`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`, W6-lite) upgrades it to `𝒪(D)`.

Because `n₁` (hence the base twist) is fixed, the effective witness carries the whole degree slack,
and `b` depends only on `(Y, π)` — exactly the shape DAT-D consumes.
-/

  -- the residual class `[D] · [F]^{-n₁}`
  set c : Y.CechPic := CurveDivisor.picClass K D
    * (CurveDivisor.picClass K (fiberWeilDivisor π) ^ n₁)⁻¹ with hc
  have hcdeg : classDeg K c

    rw [hc, classDeg_mul, classDeg_inv, classDeg_pow, classDeg_picClass, classDeg_picClass]
    ring
  -- an effective witness of the residual class
  obtain ⟨W, hWc⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K c
  have hWdeg : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) := by
    have hWeq : CurveDivisor.deg K W
        = CurveDivisor.deg K D - (n₁ : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
      rw [← hcdeg, ← hWc, classDeg_picClass]
    linarith
  obtain ⟨E, hEnonneg, hEc⟩ := exists_effective_of_picClass W hWdeg
  -- the witness divisor `n₁ • F + E` is in the class of `D`
  have hclass : CurveDivisor.picClass K (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π + E)
      = CurveDivisor.picClass K D := by
    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, picClass_nsmul, hEc, hWc, hc,
      mul_comm (CurveDivisor.picClass K D), ← mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel, one_mul]
  -- base vanishing at `n₁ • F`, peel `E`, transport along the class
  have hbase : Subsingleton
      (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1) := by
    have h := hn₁ n₁ le_rfl
    rwa [zero_add] at h

      (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π + E)) 1) :=
